requests.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset: one coherent 12-cell material-icon atlas for the cosmic combination game The Lights That Remain. A landscape 4-column by 3-row grid, equal square cells, transparent generous gutters. Exactly one circular illustration in each cell; the circle has a softly pale field and a clean complete circumference, and all space outside each circle is genuinely transparent. No labels, numbers, text, arrows, border frames, grid lines, checkerboard, UI, humans or instruments. Each circle must remain readable as an 80-pixel game icon: two or three decisive masses, broad texture, very limited small detail. Match size and lighting across the set. Subject scale changes between cells; these are illustrative selections, not one scale drawing.
Left-to-right, top-to-bottom cell order:
1. A modest orange star with five tiny widely separated cream companion points in a gently curving stream. The orange star is a compact point with a tight halo, not a large red giant or explosion.
2. The same orange star and recognizable companion group on a newly bent, more spread-out arrangement. Stars remain separate intact points. No orbit arrows.
3. An opaque forked dark gas lane across a faint broad luminous gas field. Dense gas is material obscuring light, not a black crack or empty void. No newborn stars.
4. The same lane after a gas collision: more crowded asymmetric gas knots and a denser central fork, still no stars or explosions.
5. One cream young star inside a broad inclined dusty gas disk, dark near-side notch, diffuse material with thickness. No planets, no jet, no thin Saturn rings.
6. A muted rocky world with broad impact basins and one small separate moon. No oceans or Earth continents, no rings.
7. An oblate amber gas giant with a broad pale belt, a narrow darker band and very thin inclined particulate rings. No extra moon. Keep the gas giant distinct from the young star's much broader dusty disk.
8. Three opaque dense cold cloudlets with dark interiors and irregular rounded lobes; clearly gas clouds rather than rock boulders. No stars.
9. A hot cloud disrupted into spreading ragged translucent gas strands, with an open torn silhouette. No star points, no solid fragments or flame tongues. Different shape, not merely a recolor of cell8.
10. A brilliant inclined accretion disk around a genuinely dark central region. All visible emission lies in the external disk around the dark centre. No jet, no luminous hole, no portal.
11. A narrow knotty stream of charged gas crossing an otherwise quiet circular field. Show material, not an arrow, ray symbol or line labelled as a process. No star, hole or source object in this cell.
12. A small bean-shaped rubble world with a deep notch, three major boulders and a pale wedge. It is a loose rocky aggregate, no molten core, no tail, no orbit or star. It must be recognizable after later losing its sun.

Style/medium: Luminous pastel and chalk astronomical illustration: broad softly blended volumes, controlled warm amber lights and cool blue-green shadows, opaque plum dust silhouettes, faint paper tooth, crisp tiny stellar points. Quiet, expansive and tactile; no digital lens flares or glossy 3D rendering.
